Although Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) effectively tackles Inter Symbol Interference (ISI) in multipath fading channels, its performance is reduced in high-mobility scenarios. The emerging Orthogonal Time Frequency Space (OTFS) modulation technique has demonstrated great potential in addressing these challenges. This paper delves into the analytical implications of implementing OTFS across channels experiencing both time-varying and frequency-selective fading, taking into account the more realistic scenario of rapid motion-induced Doppler scaling. The study employs the Weyl-Heisenberg basis and establishes the input-output relationship for a generalized multipath channel model. When comparing the performance of OTFS to conventional OFDM, it becomes clear that OTFS outshines its counterpart, especially in high-mobility environments. The proposed modulation scheme is assessed using simulations, demonstrating its ability to withstand channel fading and its potential for achieving high spectral efficiency. The analysis offers valuable insights into the practical implementation of OTFS in communication systems, specifically focusing on the challenges posed by fast-changing channel conditions.

articleTitle: Analyzing Performance and Efficiency in Modern Fast Fourier Transform Architechtures
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Recent Innovation in Smart and Sustainable Technology (ICRISST)
abstract: In recent technology, improvements in IC fabrications in the semiconductor industry, and most of the System on Chip integrations and communications systems, the FFT(Fast Fourier Transform)/IFFT(Inverse Fast Fourier Transform) are widely used DSP(Digital Signal Processing) techniques in the design of OFDM (Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing) and MIMO(Multiple Input Multiple Output). The major applications of FFT/IFFT are wireless, broadband, and data sharing through OFDM systems. This study introduces detailed methods for developing an FFT and IFFT core that is highly effective and designed specifically for applications that are dependent on MIMO-OFDM. In this paper, a comparative study has been done on effective and efficient methods and architecture required for FFT/IFFT, and most of the recent research has introduced mixed-radix or higher-radix methods that are suggested for MIMO and OFDM applications. This was accomplished by using an arithmetic optimization technique for radix-2 butterflies, which significantly decreased the quantity of complex multipliers needed. . In this survey paper on the replacement of the highly energy-demanding complex multipliers featured in the aforementioned radix-2 butterflies featuring high-performance approximation multipliers that have reduced failure rates and the execution of the Fast Fourier transform/inverse Fast Fourier transform model, which incorporates such improved butterflies.

articleTitle: A Review of Non-Isolated DC-DC Converter Topologies

abstract: DC-DC converters are among the most efficient power electronic devices to control DC voltage and enhancing the performance of Renewable energy systems. This paper presents a comprehensive study of various topologies of non-isolated DC-DC boost converters designed for optimal integration with photovoltaic (PV) systems.

articleTitle: Expeditious Diagnosis of Breast Cancer from Magnetic Resonance Images Using Grey Wolf Optimization based Improved K-means Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Recent Innovation in Smart and Sustainable Technology (ICRISST)
abstract: Considering early recognition can improve patient survival rates, it is one of the most crucial concerns that ought to be addressed globally. Promptly identifying any malignant cell or cells has the potential to prevent millions of deaths. Early detection of breast cancer has been achieved by the use of MRIs and mammograms; if the disease is found early, the cost of therapy can be significantly lowered. Methods for segmentation are necessary for the identification of breast cancers. In analyzing images, segmentation—which comprises identification, extraction of features, categorization, and treatment—plays a crucial role. In order to plan treatments, segmentation assists doctors in measuring the amount of tissue in the breast. Utilizing image classification techniques, one may determine the degree of cancer by analyzing the form of the malignant cells. The application of unsupervised K-Means clustering is employed to distinguish the region of interest from the background. By utilizing K-centroids, the data is segmented into K-clusters. To enhance segmentation outcomes, the Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO) is integrated with K-means. GWO is a contemporary metaheuristic swarm intelligence technique known for its notable advantages over traditional methods. Notably, it excels in the absence of derivative information during the initial search and involves minimal parameters. As a result, GWO is widely utilized for optimizing various problems.Additionally, it is straightforward, user-friendly, adaptable, scalable, and has the unique ability to manage exploration and exploitation throughout the search in a way that promotes optimal convergence. When tested on the MIAS breast cancer dataset, the hybrid GWO based enhanced K-means (GWO_iK-means) algorithm scored 93% dice score value on segmenting the infected region.

articleTitle: Optimized Security Measures: Whale-inspired Manta Ray Foraging Optimization Based Watermarking for Medical Image Data
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Recent Innovation in Smart and Sustainable Technology (ICRISST)
abstract: Localization Robust data protection protocols are necessary as the use of 3D imaging techniques in treatment and diagnosis grows. Watermarking is a crucial method in this context. The security and effectiveness of the watermarking techniques currently in use, however, have certain problems. The objective for this research is to find a new approach that can increase the durability of watermarking for 3D medical data as well as fortify defenses against unauthorized access and manipulation. In this paper, we present a novel whale-inspired manta ray foraging optimization (W-MRFO) method for achieving the ideal balance between invisibility and insertion capacity. By refining the watermark insertion process, the system aims to strike a balance between personal and analytic image reliability, taking cues from the agile foraging activities of manta rays and the collaborative actions of whale groups. We evaluate the proposed W-MRFO approach on a comprehensive set of 3D imaging samples. The application of linear discriminant analysis (LDA) to minimize the dimension could reduce inaccuracy. The recommended W-MRFO approach is implemented and the effectiveness of the watermarking is examined, using a Python program. The outcomes demonstrate how well the recommended technique for watermarking clinical images performs, providing robust protection against alteration and unauthorized access.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Different Resource Allocation Schemes used for Carrier Aggregation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Recent Innovation in Smart and Sustainable Technology (ICRISST)
abstract: This paper examines Carrier Aggregation (CA) techniques in mobile networks, crucial for achieving high data rates despite spectrum fragmentation. The study delves into the evolution of mobile networks from 1G to 5G, highlighting the significance of each generation in reshaping mobile communications. Carrier Aggregation introduced in LTE-Advanced and continued in 5G, enables the aggregation of multiple component carriers (CCs) to attain higher data rates. The paper discusses various CC and Resource Block (RB) allocation schemes, categorizing them based on their allocation strategies, such as Round Robin, Random, and Hashing algorithms. Additionally, it explores joint CC and RB allocation methods, demonstrating their superiority over disjoint schemes in enhancing user throughput and fairness. The research presents comparative analyses and evaluations of these schemes, outlining their impact on system performance metrics like throughput, coverage, packet loss rate, fairness index, and UE power consumption. Finally, the paper concludes that joint allocation schemes exhibit superior performance compared to individual allocation strategies, with certain algorithms standing out for their efficiency in optimizing user throughput and power consumption for low latency applications.

articleTitle: Covert Cryptography in Pixel Realms: Unveiling Nonlinear-Encrypted Generative Adversarial Networks for Stealthy Image Steganography
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Recent Innovation in Smart and Sustainable Technology (ICRISST)
abstract: This article introduces an innovative grayscale image steganography approach competent of concealing confidential data within a carrier image of the corresponding dimensions. The method involves encrypting the confidential image using nonlinear encryption technology before embedding it. A convolutional neural network is then employed to transform the encrypted and carrier images into a concealed image. Furthermore, a GAN-generative adversarial network is utilized to generate a closer to reality concealed image, making it challenging to differentiate from the original carrier image. The steganography framework is constructed using three Convolutional Neural Networks acting as the concealment network, differentiative network, and retrieving network, correspondingly. Furthermore, a novel weight assignment process is initiated to verify a balanced development process for the concealment-retrieving networks. The empirical findings demonstrate that this suggested framework not just resolves issues related to covert data compromise and manipulation found in present dominant approaches as well maintains a ample concealing capability. Comparative analysis in conjunction with present methods shows that the mean Embedding rate, PSNR and Structural Similarity Index of the concealed images generated using this scheme reach 9.03, 30.982 and 0.844, respectively. The precision of the restoration of confidential images is notably superior.

articleTitle: Blockchain and Machine Learning Integration for Secure Data Exchange in Modern Digital Ecosystems

abstract: In response to the growing demand for safe data exchange in modern digital ecosystems, the study analyzes the combination of blockchain with machine learning, proposing a unique framework to solve the limitations of existing systems. Existing systems have drawbacks such as compromised data integrity, vulnerability to illegal access, and a lack of fundamental trust mechanisms. The proposed system combines the reliability of blockchain with the analytical capabilities of machine learning, strengthening data security and privacy. Using blockchain’s decentralized ledger provides transparency and integrity, while machine learning algorithms contribute predictive analytics and anomaly identification. Through extensive testing and analysis, the proposed system indicates significant improvements in avoiding unwanted access and maintaining data accuracy. The results highlight the revolutionary potential of the integration across multiple industries, minimizing the constraints of outdated technologies and building a stronger and trustworthy environment for data exchange. The study offers critical insights to the growing environment of secure data exchange, paving the way for companies to embrace a future where privacy and dependability are essential.

articleTitle: Mental Health Analysis using Machine Learning Techniques

abstract: Mental illness is a global health problem that affects the health of millions of people all over the world. Early detection and management of these diseases is important to improve patient outcomes. Machine learning technologies have become powerful tools for clinical psychology, offering the potential to revolutionize diagnosis, treatment, and support for people affected by these issues. This research provides an overview of recent advances in psychological analysis using machine learning. This research examines the latest techniques and use of machine learning in psychological analysis. Health analytics from multiple data sources, including electronic health records, brain imaging data, and wearable data. This discuss the integration of advanced screening with conventional screening to increase the accuracy and efficiency of diagnoses such as depression, anxiety, schizophrenia, autism, and bipolar disorder. More importantly, predictive models are explored for early diagnosis and personalized treatment recommendations, demonstrating the potential to reduce treatment burden and improve patient care. This also share these ethical principles regarding mental health information, privacy, and treatment. The possibility of algorithmic bias highlights the importance of building a transparent and unbiased model. It also dive into ongoing research and initiatives to alleviate these concerns. This review highlights the important role of machine learning in improving mental health by improving diagnosis, early recognition, self-correction, and support. Advances in mental health technology have the potential to change the way of view and respond to mental health problems, ultimately improving the lives of those affected by the condition.

articleTitle: Unlocking the Mysteries of the Deep: Leveraging the Power of MobileNet and YOLOv5 for Efficient and Accurate Sea Cucumber Detection in Underwater Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Recent Innovation in Smart and Sustainable Technology (ICRISST)
abstract: In the realm of marine biology and underwater research, the discovery and understanding of marine species play a pivotal role in unraveling the mysteries of the deep ocean. This research endeavors to advance the field by harnessing the capabilities of deep learning through the fusion of MobileNet and YOLOv5, two cutting-edge neural network architectures. This study focuses on sea cucumber detection, a task vital for ecosystem assessment, biodiversity studies, and habitat analysis. MobileNet, known for its efficiency and compactness, is employed for feature extraction, while YOLOv5, recognized for its real-time object detection prowess, is adapted for classification. By synergizing these models, authors achieve a highly efficient and accurate sea cucumber detection system tailored to the challenges of underwater environments. This research introduces a meticulously curated dataset comprising sea cucumber images sourced from various underwater ecosystems, offering a comprehensive representation of these enigmatic creatures. Authors present a detailed methodology for data preprocessing, including Gray-Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM) analysis for texture features, and image augmentation techniques to enhance model robustness using Google Images. Subsequently, the fusion of MobileNet and YOLOv5 capitalizes on MobileNet's ability to extract discriminative features efficiently and YOLOv5's real-time detection capabilities. The experimental results showcase remarkable accuracy and efficiency in sea cucumber detection, exceeding the performance of traditional methods and single-model approaches with accuracy of 97.39%. The proposed system not only accurately classifies sea cucumber species but also provides valuable insights into their ecological roles and habitats.
